findings.title: Feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized same-origin HTML
findings.body: The new raw_html cook method returns raw source without passing it through the normal cooking/sanitizing pipeline. PollFeed supplies untrusted feed entry content (and explicitly CGI-unescapes it) to TopicEmbed.import, which creates posts with this mode; script tags, event-handler attributes, and dangerous URLs can therefore be stored in cooked and rendered with raw in the embed and normal topic views. A compromised or malicious configured feed can execute JavaScript in the Discourse origin for every viewer. Sanitize imported HTML with a strict allowlist before persisting/rendering it rather than bypassing the cooker.

findings.title: The embeddable-host check is bypassed by HTTP redirects
findings.body: TopicRetriever validates only the hostname in the original embed URL, but open(url) follows redirects without rechecking the destination. A URL on the configured embeddable host can redirect the server to localhost, a cloud metadata endpoint, or another internal service; the fetched response is then imported into a topic and can be read through the embed endpoint. Disable redirects or validate the scheme, host, and port of every redirect target before fetching.

findings.title: Remote retrieval depends on open-uri without requiring it
findings.body: import_remote calls open on an HTTP URL but neither this file nor TopicRetriever requires open-uri. PollFeed requires it only if that scheduled-job class happens to be loaded; with feed polling disabled, the normal RetrieveTopic path can reach this method with Kernel#open still handling URLs as file paths and fail with ENOENT. Require open-uri in the component that performs the remote fetch.

findings.title: Post-processing jobs are enqueued before the enclosing import transaction commits
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create in an outer Topic.transaction. PostCreator enqueues its process-post and feature-topic jobs after its own nested transaction, but Rails joins that nested transaction to this still-open outer transaction. A worker can therefore run before the topic, post, and TopicEmbed are committed; if TopicEmbed.create! later loses the unique-index race, the database work is rolled back while the already-enqueued jobs remain. Enqueue these jobs after the outer transaction commits (for example via an after_commit callback).

findings.title: A valid feed entry without content aborts the entire polling job
findings.body: i.content is optional in both RSS and Atom feeds; many RSS feeds expose description and many Atom feeds expose summary instead. Calling scrub on a missing content value raises NoMethodError, and this job has retries disabled, so the remaining entries are skipped until a later scheduled run. Handle absent content safely and fall back to the appropriate description/summary field or skip the entry.

findings.title: postMessage origin validation accepts prefix origins
findings.body: The handler checks whether e.origin is a substring of discourseUrl instead of comparing origins. For example, when discourseUrl is https://forum.example.com/, a window from attacker-controlled https://forum.example.co passes this check and can send a discourse-resize message to a page it opens, forcing the embedded iframe to an arbitrary height. Parse discourseUrl and require an exact origin match, preferably also requiring e.source to be the iframe's contentWindow.

findings.title: Only root-relative URLs are rewritten in imported HTML
findings.body: absolutize_urls claims to convert relative URLs, but it rewrites only values beginning with /. Common relative links such as images/photo.jpg, ../photo.jpg, and ?page=2 remain unchanged and are resolved by the browser against the Discourse embed URL rather than the source article, breaking imported links and images. Resolve all relative href/src values against the article URL (for example with URI.join).

findings.title: The Disqus import command no longer accepts its documented category option
findings.body: Removing method_option :category makes existing invocations using --category fail as an unknown Thor switch, and there is no replacement for selecting a category for imported threads. This is a backwards-incompatible change to an administrative CLI contract and should either continue passing the category through the TopicEmbed import path or be intentionally deprecated and documented.

findings.title: Disqus thread creation timestamps are no longer preserved
findings.body: The previous PostCreator call passed Date.parse(t[:created_at]) when creating each imported thread. The replacement TopicEmbed.import_remote call accepts only the title here and TopicEmbed.import does not forward a created_at option, so every imported topic receives the import time instead of its original Disqus creation time. This changes topic ordering and loses migration metadata; add and pass through a created_at option.
